pending_commit.commit_message: login: Force crashpad on kukui Force kukui devices to start using crashpad immediately. Breakpad does not work on kukui devices such as Krane. We are losing crash reports from Chrome browser processes, and other Chrome crash reports are corrupt and unusable. This is a launch blocker for Krane; we don't know if there are stability issues. Crashpad does not have the same issues as breakpad on these devices. We want to move to crashpad eventually anyways, so rather than trying to fix the deprecated breakpad, let's move to crashpad on kukui. There are no released kukui devices, so this only affects testers. Other devices do not have the same issues with breakpad, so we can do a slower rollout & dogfooding for everything else in later CLs. This is just the emergency switchover for kukui. BUG=chromium:1001139 TEST=On a Krane. kill -SEGV main chrome process. Visit chrome://crash, chrome://gpucrash, and chrome://inducebrowsercrashforrealz. All produce crash reports. FROMGIT: firmware: google: check if size is valid when decoding VPD data The VPD implementation from Chromium Vital Product Data project used to parse data from untrusted input without checking if the meta data is invalid or corrupted. For example, the size from decoded content may be negative value, or larger than whole input buffer. Such invalid data may cause buffer overflow. To fix that, the size parameters passed to vpd_decode functions should be changed to unsigned integer (u32) type, and the parsing of entry header should be refactored so every size field is correctly verified before starting to decode. BUG=chromium:967209 TEST=emerge-kukui chromeos-kernel-4_19 Fixes: ad2ac9d5c5e0 ("firmware: Google VPD: import lib_vpd source files") Signed-off-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net> Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org> Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190830022402.214442-1-hungte@chromium.org Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org> (cherry picked from commit 4b708b7b1a2c09fbdfff6b942ebe3a160213aacd git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/gregkh/char-misc.git char-misc-next) Cq-Depend: chromium:1832656 Change-Id: Iebc51abeba143719d0bb55e78e9048aca559c3b8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1795465 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: firmware: google: increment VPD key_len properly Commit 4b708b7b1a2c ("firmware: google: check if size is valid when decoding VPD data") adds length checks, but the new vpd_decode_entry() function botched the logic -- it adds the key length twice, instead of adding the key and value lengths separately. On my local system, this means vpd.c's vpd_section_create_attribs() hits an error case after the first attribute it parses, since it's no longer looking at the correct offset. With this patch, I'm back to seeing all the correct attributes in /sys/firmware/vpd/... CHROMIUM: fix up logic bug in chromiumos LSM This LSM does multiple security checks when userspace calls setuid, setreuid or setresuid. Make sure not to return early if one of the checks passes, since the others could still fail. Without doing this, userspace can trivially bypass the CAP_SETUID hardening logic. BUG=chromium:845640 TEST=security_ProcessManagementPolicy Signed-off-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Change-Id: I59d2ffdc11c21b49fd08e8714a0265419c693884 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1566032 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

FIXUP: FROMGIT: patman: Use the Change-Id, version, and prefix in the Message-Id === This is a squash of a revert of the FROMLIST patch we landed earlier with a pick of the FROMGIT patch. === As per the centithread on ksummit-discuss [1], there are folks who feel that if a Change-Id is present in a developer's local commit that said Change-Id could be interesting to include in upstream posts. Specifically if two commits are posted with the same Change-Id there's a reasonable chance that they are either the same commit or a newer version of the same commit. Specifically this is because that's how gerrit has trained people to work. There is much angst about Change-Id in upstream Linux, but one thing that seems safe and non-controversial is to include the Change-Id as part of the string of crud that makes up a Message-Id. Let's give that a try. In theory (if there is enough adoption) this could help a tool more reliably find various versions of a commit. This actually might work pretty well for U-Boot where (I believe) quite a number of developers use patman, so there could be critical mass (assuming that enough of these people also use a git hook that adds Change-Id to their commits). I was able to find this git hook by searching for "gerrit change id git hook" in my favorite search engine. In theory one could imagine something like this could be integrated into other tools, possibly even git-send-email. Getting it into patman seems like a sane first step, though. NOTE: this patch is being posted using a patman containing this patch, so you should be able to see the Message-Id of this patch and see that it contains my local Change-Id, which ends in 2b9 if you want to check. [1] https://lists.linuxfoundation.org/pipermail/ksummit-discuss/2019-August/006739.html Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit 858a7f2484992667fe9bcf959123bea201c59904 https://gitlab.denx.de/u-boot/custodians/u-boot-dm.git next) BUG=None TEST=Use patman to send this patch Change-Id: I55f8465574089894a732fa2f0075984925976e83 Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1832143 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Simon Glass <sjg@chromium.org>
